explanation: The March 22 document contains multiple substantive elements that could plausibly explain a market structural break around March 27: it formally acknowledged that banking-sector developments (SVB/Signature fallout) would 'result in tighter credit conditions' and 'weigh on economic activity,' delivered a 25bp hike to 4.75-5%, and critically shifted forward guidance language from 'ongoing increases will be appropriate' to 'some additional policy firming may be appropriate'—a notable dovish pivot in trajectory signaling that the tightening cycle was nearing its end. The minutes' release (typically ~3 weeks after the meeting, i.e., around March 22 statement date) and subsequent Fed communications in the days following could have crystallized market repricing of the terminal rate path, consistent with a structural break on March 27.
